mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of FEDFUNDS decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of UNRATE increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of INDPRO decrease.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in the last month, it signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decrease.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter indicates a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained GDPC1 increase.
